mainTopic: Rescuing sacred writings from a fire on שבת: foreign languages, blessings and amulets, improper ink, and the 85-letter minimum for a worn ספר תורה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a search for which תנאים argue the same way as רב הונא and רב חסדא about rescuing כתבי הקודש written in other languages. The answer is רבי יוסי against the תנא who rules about Coptic writing. A ברייתא then rules that written blessings and amulets are not rescued on שבת, even though they contain God's Name. A story follows in which רבי ישמעאל rebukes a scribe who sank such texts in water. The ריש גלותא asks about writings in לשון הקודש that were written in improper ink. Based on a ברייתא brought by רב אשי, the conclusion is that they are rescued. רב נחמן rules that a worn ספר תורה from which 85 letters cannot be gathered is not rescued, and he defends that ruling against a challenge from the Aramaic phrase יגר שהדותא. רב הונא and רב חסדא then argue about whether the 85 letters must be together or may be scattered. The amud ends by beginning a ברייתא about the special signs around ויהי בנסוע הארון, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Suggesting the תנא קמא as the one who argues with רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא who argues with רבי יוסי reflects the same dispute as רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the first תנא who argues with רבי יוסי...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still searching for a תנאים dispute that matches the argument between רב הונא and רב חסדא. Here it proposes one candidate, and the next step will test that proposal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked which תנא disagrees with רבי יוסי on rescuing writings in foreign languages. The first suggestion is the תנא קמא of that same ברייתא. This is only an opening proposal.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)
The first, anonymous תנא in a teaching

phrases.english: If you say it is the first Tanna who argues with Rabbi Yosei —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier search for a תנאים source matching רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: That the רב הונא and רב חסדא dispute matches a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the תנא קמא against רבי יוסי

steps.title: Their dispute may be about something else: may these books be read?
steps.stepSummary: The proposal is rejected because the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי may be arguing about whether such books may be read at all, not about rescuing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they argue about this: one Master holds these writings were given to be read, and the other Master holds they were not given to be read.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 1. The two תנאים might be arguing about a different issue entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא and רב חסדא both agree that foreign-language writings may not be read; their argument is only about rescuing them. If the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי argue about whether reading is allowed, their dispute is not the same as ours, so it is no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: They were given to be read from

phrases.english: But perhaps they argue about this:
One Master holds: they were given to be read from,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לֹא נִיתְּנוּ לִקְרוֹת בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: and the other Master holds: they were not given to be read from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the identification with the תנא קמא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Their dispute may concern whether reading is allowed, not whether the writings are rescued.

steps.title: The real disputants: רבי יוסי and the תנא of Coptic
steps.stepSummary: The matching dispute is between רבי יוסי and the תנא who rules about writings in Coptic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the dispute is between רבי יוסי and the תנא who spoke about Coptic writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer about which תנאים match רב הונא and רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא of Coptic holds that even writings which may not be read are still rescued. רבי יוסי holds they are not rescued. This is a dispute about rescuing alone, so it matches the אמוראים' argument exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Coptic, an Egyptian language and script

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Yosei and the Tanna of Coptic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion with a correct one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the identification of the disputants
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא argues with רבי יוסי about rescuing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא of Coptic, who rescues even writings that may not be read, argues with רבי יוסי.
steps.whatToRemember: The רב הונא and רב חסדא dispute about rescuing foreign-language writings matches the dispute between רבי יוסי and the תנא of Coptic.

steps.title: Written blessings and amulets are not rescued from fire
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that written blessings and amulets are not rescued from a fire on שבת, even though they contain God's Name and Torah material.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: blessings and amulets, even though they contain letters of God's Name and many passages from the Torah, are not rescued from a fire. Rather, they burn where they are, together with the Names in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about another kind of writing: written blessings and קמיעות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the presence of שמות would require saving them. The ברייתא rules that these texts lack the status of כתבי הקודש. So they are left to burn on שבת, Names included.

keyTerms.meaning: Written texts of blessings and prayers
Amulets containing written verses or Names
Rescuing from a fire on שבת

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: blessings and amulets,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁל שֵׁם
phrases.english: even though they contain letters of the Name
and many passages that are in the Torah —
are not rescued from the fire,
rather, they burn in their place,
they and the Names in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about which writings are rescued.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Written blessings and amulets are not rescued on שבת, even with God's Name in them.

steps.title: Writers of blessings are like burners of Torah
steps.stepSummary: From this ruling the חכמים concluded that people who write blessings are like people who burn Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: those who write blessings are like those who burn the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a moral lesson from the ruling in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These texts will be left to burn on שבת, Names and all. So whoever writes them is in effect setting up God's Name to be destroyed. That is why the writer is compared to someone who burns Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (a lesson drawn from the ruling)

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: כּוֹתְבֵי בְרָכוֹת כְּשׂוֹרְפֵי תוֹרָה.
phrases.english: From here they said: writers of blessings are like burners of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: כּוֹתְבֵי בְרָכוֹת כְּשׂוֹרְפֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a lesson from the ruling in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Writing blessings is discouraged because it exposes God's Name to destruction.

steps.title: The scribe in Sidon hides his blessings in water
steps.stepSummary: A scribe in Sidon who wrote blessings saw רבי ישמעאל coming and hid his bundle of blessings by sinking it in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man in Sidon who wrote blessings. People came and told רבי ישמעאל, and רבי ישמעאל went to check on him. As he was climbing the ladder, the man sensed him coming. He took a bundle of blessings and sank it in a basin of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story connected to the lesson about writing blessings. This sets up רבי ישמעאל's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scribe knew that writing blessings was frowned upon. To hide the evidence, he did something even worse: he submerged texts with God's Name, which erases them.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle or roll of pages

phrases.english: An incident with one who was writing in Sidon;
they came and informed Rabbi Yishmael,
and Rabbi Yishmael went to examine him.
As he was going up the ladder, the man sensed him,
took a bundle of blessings
and sank them in a basin of water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the lesson of step 5 with a story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story that illustrates the disapproval of writing blessings.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the second sin is worse than the first
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל told the scribe that the punishment for destroying the blessings is greater than the punishment for writing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with these words רבי ישמעאל said to him: the punishment for the last act is greater than for the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי ישמעאל's rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing blessings was the first wrong. Sinking them in water, which erases God's Name with his own hands, is the second and more serious wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter more than the former

phrases.aramaic: וּבַלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: And in these words Rabbi Yishmael said to him:
The punishment for the latter is greater than for the former.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with its punchline.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Writing blessings is wrong, but actively erasing God's Name is even worse.
steps.whatToRemember: Blessings and amulets are not rescued on שבת, and writing them is discouraged. Destroying a Name directly is worse than writing such texts.

steps.title: The ריש גלותא asks about לשון הקודש writings in improper ink
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא asks רבה בר רב הונא whether sacred writings in לשון הקודש, but written with non-permanent inks, are rescued from a fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ריש גלותא asked רבה בר רב הונא: if the writings were written with arsenic, red paint, gum, or iron sulfate, but in לשון הקודש, are they rescued from the fire or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. The writing is in the correct language, but the ink is not proper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case has one good feature (the holy language) and one weak feature (ink that does not last). The question is which feature decides.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Babylonian Jewish community
Arsenic-based yellow paint and red paint

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא מֵרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: The Exilarch asked Rabba bar Rav Huna:
If they were written in arsenic or red paint,
in gum or iron sulfate, in the holy tongue,

phrases.aramaic: מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה אוֹ אֵין מַצִּילִין?
phrases.english: does one rescue them from the fire or not rescue them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא מֵרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new inquiry about a writing in the right language but the wrong ink.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether non-permanent ink cancels the rescue status of a holy-tongue writing

steps.title: The question applies according to both opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this question arises both for the view that rescues foreign-language writings and for the view that does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question can be asked according to the one who says they are rescued, and according to the one who says they are not rescued.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next two steps. It announces that the question is relevant to both sides of the רב הונא and רב חסדא dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a question fits only one opinion. Here the case mixes a stronger feature (the language) with a weaker one (the ink), so it is unclear under both views.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: It is a question according to the one who says one rescues,
it is a question according to the one who says one does not rescue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Frames the scope of the question in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Showing that the doubt exists under both opinions

steps.title: Even the strict view might rescue holy-tongue writings
steps.stepSummary: The one who does not rescue foreign-language writings might still rescue these, because they are written in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a question for the one who says they are not rescued: perhaps that applies only where they are written in translation or another language, but here, where they are in לשון הקודש, they are rescued.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the strict opinion might still rescue in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict opinion's reason may have been the foreign language. Here the language is correct, so that reason does not apply, and the bad ink may not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in a specific case)

phrases.english: It is a question according to the one who says one does not rescue:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיבִי תַּרְגּוּם וּבְכָל לָשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: perhaps that applies where they are written in translation or any language,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא דִּכְתִיבִי בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ — מַצִּילִין,
phrases.english: but here, where they are written in the holy tongue, one rescues;

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּיבְּעֵי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מַצִּילִין — הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיבִי תַּרְגּוּם וּבְכָל לָשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side announced in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the strict view's concern is only about language

steps.title: Even the lenient view might not rescue writings in poor ink
steps.stepSummary: The one who rescues foreign-language writings might not rescue these, because the ink does not last.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps, even according to the one who says they are rescued, that applies only where they are written in ink that lasts. But here, since it does not last, they are not rescued.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side: why the lenient opinion might not rescue in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient opinion may require a lasting writing. Ink that fades makes the text temporary, so it may not deserve rescue even in the holy language.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מַצִּילִין —
phrases.english: or perhaps even according to the one who says one rescues,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיבִי בִּדְיוֹ דְּמִיקַּיַּים,
phrases.english: that applies where they are written in ink that endures,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא כֵּיוָן דְּלָא מִיקַּיַּים — לָא.
phrases.english: but here, since it does not endure, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מַצִּילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second side announced in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the lenient view requires permanent ink

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: they are not rescued
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא answers that such writings are not rescued.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: they are not rescued.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives his ruling on the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He holds that the poor ink decides the case. Writing that does not last loses its rescue status even in לשון הקודש.

phrases.english: He said to him: One does not rescue them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 8 through 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Writings in non-permanent ink are not rescued.

steps.title: Challenge from רב המנונא's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ריש גלותא objects that רב המנונא taught a ברייתא saying such writings are rescued.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב המנונא taught that they are rescued!
steps.whatsHappening: The ריש גלותא challenges the answer with a tannaitic source that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא cannot rule against a ברייתא. So רבה בר רב הונא's ruling seems to be contradicted.

phrases.english: But Rav Hamnuna taught that one rescues!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that they are not rescued
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא recited by רב המנונא explicitly rules that they are rescued.

steps.title: If it was taught, it was taught
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא accepts the ברייתא and retracts his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: if it was taught in a ברייתא, then it was taught.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of defending his view, רבה בר רב הונא gives in to the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase means: if there really is such a ברייתא, I accept it and withdraw my ruling. The law becomes that these writings are rescued.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was taught, it was taught (I accept it)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a defense of his ruling. It is a concession that reverses it.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it was taught, it was taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by conceding.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following the ברייתא, they are rescued.

steps.title: Which ברייתא is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברייתא teaches that such writings are rescued.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the ברייתא that was taught?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source text behind רב המנונא's teaching. The next step will supply it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ברייתא was only mentioned, never quoted. The גמרא wants to see where the law is actually shown.

phrases.english: What was taught?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the text of the ברייתא mentioned in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The ברייתא showing that writings in improper ink are rescued

steps.title: רב אשי: only a מגילה requires ink
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי cites a ברייתא showing that only מגילת אסתר must be written in ink, so other ספרים remain holy without it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: as it was taught, the only difference between ספרים and a מגילה is that ספרים may be written in any language, while a מגילה must be in Assyrian script, on a scroll, and in ink.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי identifies the source. Requiring ink for the מגילה alone implies that other holy books keep their status without proper ink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ink were required for all holy books, the ברייתא could not list it as a difference. So books written in other materials are still holy, and they are rescued on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: As it was taught:
There is no difference between books and the Megillah
except that books are written in any language,
and a Megillah only once it is written in Assyrian script,
on a scroll, and in ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by supplying the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא requires ink only for a מגילה, implying other ספרים are holy and rescued even without proper ink.
steps.whatToRemember: Sacred writings in לשון הקודש are rescued even when written in non-permanent ink, because only a מגילה requires ink.

steps.title: A worn ספר תורה from which 85 letters cannot be gathered
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חלוב asks רב נחמן whether a ספר תורה from which one cannot gather 85 letters, the length of ויהי בנסוע הארון, is rescued.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חלוב asked רב נחמן: a ספר תורה from which you cannot gather 85 letters, like the section of ויהי בנסוע הארון, is it rescued from the fire or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins, about a ספר תורה that is badly worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eighty-five letters, the size of ויהי בנסוע הארון, is the minimum for a text to hold the holiness of a ספר תורה. The question is whether a scroll that no longer has this much intact text still deserves rescue.

keyTerms.meaning: The two-verse section in במדבר of 85 letters

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חֲלוּב מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥaluv asked Rav Naḥman:
A Torah scroll in which there is not enough to compile
eighty-five letters,
like the portion of 'And when the Ark traveled',

phrases.aramaic: מַצִּילִין אוֹתָן מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה, אוֹ אֵין מַצִּילִין?
phrases.english: does one rescue it from the fire, or not rescue it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חֲלוּב מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new inquiry about minimum size.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a ספר תורה from which 85 letters cannot be gathered is rescued

steps.title: רב נחמן: why not ask about the section itself?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן responds by asking why he does not also ask about the section of ויהי בנסוע itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: then ask also about the section of ויהי בנסוע הארון itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back on how the question was framed, suggesting it should cover the section itself too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן seems to understand the question as being about a text slightly short of 85 letters. If so, the same doubt should apply to an incomplete ויהי בנסוע section.

phrases.english: He said to him: Then ask
about the portion of 'And when the Ark traveled' itself?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְתִיבְּעֵי לָךְ פָּרָשַׁת וַיְהִי בִּנְסוֹעַ הָאָרוֹן גּוּפַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the framing of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of רב הונא בר חלוב's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the issue is falling short of 85 letters, it should equally apply to the incomplete section itself.

steps.title: An incomplete section with God's Names is surely rescued
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חלוב explains that an incomplete ויהי בנסוע section is clearly rescued, because it contains God's Names.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where the section of ויהי בנסוע is missing letters, I have no question. Since it contains mentions of God's Name, it is rescued even without 85 letters.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חלוב clarifies that his question was never about the section itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section contains שמות, and that alone is enough reason to rescue it. So the 85-letter issue matters only for text without such Names.

keyTerms.meaning: I have no question about it

phrases.english: Where the portion of 'And when it traveled' is incomplete,
it is not a question for me,
since it contains mentions of the Name,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ שְׁמוֹנִים וְחָמֵשׁ אוֹתִיּוֹת —
phrases.english: even though it does not have eighty-five letters,
one rescues it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּחָסַר פָּרָשַׁת וַיְהִי בִּנְסוֹעַ — לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's pushback in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the scope of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question covers an incomplete ויהי בנסוע section.
steps.terutzMaskana: That section is rescued because of its Names; the question is about something else.

steps.title: The real question: a worn scroll with too little text
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חלוב restates his question: what is the law for a ספר תורה from which 85 letters cannot be gathered?
steps.simpleTranslation: What I am asking about is a ספר תורה from which you cannot gather 85 letters. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Having cleared up the confusion, רב הונא בר חלוב states his real question again. This prepares for רב נחמן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The focus is a worn scroll from which 85 letters cannot be gathered, presumably without Names. The issue is whether being part of a ספר תורה is enough by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: What I am asking about is

phrases.english: Where it is a question for me

phrases.aramaic: סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ לְלַקֵּט, מַאי?
phrases.english: is a Torah scroll with not enough to compile; what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ לְלַקֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the original question after the clarification.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The law for a worn ספר תורה from which 85 letters cannot be gathered

steps.title: רב נחמן: it is not rescued
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that such a worn ספר תורה is not rescued from the fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is not rescued.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the final answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 85 letters cannot be gathered, and there are no Names, the remains no longer carry the holiness of a ספר תורה for this purpose. So they are not rescued on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: A ספר תורה too worn to yield 85 letters is not rescued on שבת. A section with God's Names is rescued even if it is short of 85 letters. Whether the 85 letters must be together is discussed in steps 24-27.

phrases.english: He said to him: One does not rescue it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the restated question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ספר תורה without 85 gatherable letters is not rescued.

steps.title: A Short Aramaic Verse Seems to Be Saved Without 85 Letters
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חלוב challenges רב נחמן from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says Aramaic passages in תנ"ך are saved from a fire, including the tiny Aramaic phrase יגר שהדותא in the Torah, even though it has far fewer than 85 letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'A תרגום passage written in Hebrew, a Hebrew passage written as תרגום, and a scroll written in כתב עברית are all saved from a fire. Certainly the תרגום sections in עזרא, in דניאל, and in the Torah are saved. What is the תרגום in the Torah? It is יגר שהדותא. And it is saved even though it does not contain 85 letters!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חלוב brings a ברייתא to attack רב נחמן's ruling that a worn ספר תורה without 85 letters is not saved. The ברייתא seems to say that even a two-word Aramaic phrase is saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said a piece of Torah needs at least 85 letters, the length of ויהי בנסוע, to be saved from a fire. The ברייתא lists the Aramaic phrase in the Torah, יגר שהדותא, among the things that are saved. That phrase is clearly much shorter than 85 letters, so the ברייתא seems to contradict רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Aramaic translation, or a passage originally written in Aramaic
The ancient Hebrew script, not the standard כתב אשורית
'Mound of testimony', the Aramaic name לבן gave the pile of stones (בראשית לא:מז)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two meanings of תרגום here. In the first lines it means a passage that is normally Aramaic. In 'תרגום שבתורה' it refers to the actual Aramaic words that appear inside the Torah itself.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Aramaic translation that one wrote in Hebrew,
and Hebrew Scripture that one wrote in Aramaic,
and something written in ancient Hebrew script —
we rescue them from the fire.
And needless to say,
the Aramaic in Ezra, in Daniel, and in the Torah.
What is the Aramaic that is in the Torah? —
"Yegar Sahaduta" (Genesis 31:47),
phrases.notes: Only two words, far fewer than 85 letters.

phrases.english: and this is so even though it does not contain
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's own sharpening of the challenge.

phrases.english: eighty-five letters!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling in step 21 that fewer than 85 letters are not saved.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that a worn ספר תורה needs 85 letters to be saved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא saves the Aramaic יגר שהדותא, which has far fewer than 85 letters. This shows that fewer than 85 letters can still be saved.

steps.title: The Aramaic Phrase Only Helps Complete the 85
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the ברייתא is not saying יגר שהדותא is saved on its own. It means those Aramaic words count toward completing the total of 85 letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it meant that the Aramaic words count to complete the 85.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his rule by reinterpreting the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the ברייתא is that Aramaic words inside the Torah still count as Torah text. So if a scrap has יגר שהדותא plus enough Hebrew letters around it, the Aramaic letters join in to reach 85. The 85-letter minimum stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: When it was taught (meaning, what the ברייתא was really talking about)

phrases.english: When that baraita was taught —
it was to complete (the eighty-five letters).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא saves the short Aramaic phrase even when it stands alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Aramaic only counts toward the 85-letter total, so רב נחמן's minimum stands.

steps.title: Must the 85 Letters Be Together or May They Be Scattered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new question: must the 85 letters be in one connected block, or may they be spread across the worn scroll?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: these 85 letters, must they be gathered together, or may they even be scattered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about how the 85-letter rule works in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the 85-letter minimum is accepted, the question is how the letters must appear. Either they must form one continuous stretch, like the section ויהי בנסוע itself, or they may be counted from different places in the scroll.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
These eighty-five letters,
must they be together, or (may they even be) scattered?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 85-letter rule that was just defended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 85 letters must be in one continuous place or may be counted from scattered spots.

steps.title: רב הונא Says Together, רב חסדא Says Even Scattered
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree. רב הונא requires the letters to be together. רב חסדא allows even scattered letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: they must be together. רב חסדא said: even if they are scattered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opposing answers to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that only a connected stretch of 85 letters still looks like a real piece of Torah. רב חסדא holds that the total count is what matters, even if the letters come from different places.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: together.
Rav Ḥisda said: even scattered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 with a disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: only letters that are together count. רב חסדא: scattered letters also count.

steps.title: The Word 'To Gather' Seems to Refute רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a worn ספר תורה is saved if one can 'gather' 85 letters from it. Gathering suggests the letters are scattered, which seems to refute רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a worn ספר תורה, if one can gather 85 letters from it, like the section ויהי בנסוע הארון, is saved. If not, it is not saved. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to prove רב חסדא right and רב הונא wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is ללקט, 'to gather'. You only need to gather letters if they are spread out. So the ברייתא seems to count scattered letters, against רב הונא, who requires them to be together.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A Torah scroll that has worn out,
if there is in it enough to gather
eighty-five letters,
like the section "And when the Ark traveled" — we rescue it,
and if not — we do not rescue it.
A refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's position from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that the 85 letters must be together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word ללקט means gathering from different places, so scattered letters count.

steps.title: רב חסדא Defends רב הונא: Scattered Whole Words
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains the ברייתא in a way that fits רב הונא. The 'gathering' is of whole words found in different places, not loose single letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it according to רב הונא: it is talking about words.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered, and surprisingly רב חסדא himself defends his opponent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רב הונא agrees that complete words spread through the scroll can be gathered toward 85 letters. Their real disagreement is only about loose, isolated letters. So the ברייתא does not refute רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not changing his own opinion. He is only showing that the ברייתא can also fit רב הונא's view, so it is no proof against him.
steps.whatToRemember: 85 letters are needed to save a worn ספר תורה. Scattered whole words count according to everyone. The dispute between רב הונא and רב חסדא is only about scattered single letters.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda interpreted it
according to the view of Rav Huna:
(it speaks of letters scattered) in whole words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב חִסְדָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Gathering' means collecting loose scattered letters, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Gathering' means collecting whole words, which רב הונא accepts. The dispute is limited to loose letters.

steps.title: God Placed Signs Around the Section of ויהי בנסוע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a ברייתא about the section ויהי בנסוע הארון. God made special markers before and after it, and the ברייתא is about to explain why.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And when the Ark traveled, משה said.' For this section, הקדוש ברוך הוא made signs above and below it, to say...
steps.whatsHappening: Since ויהי בנסוע was just mentioned, the גמרא starts a new ברייתא about it. The reason for the markers continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section is set off by special signs, written as reversed נוני״ן, before and after it. The word לומר shows that an explanation of their purpose is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: Above and below (before and after the section)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And when the Ark traveled, Moses said" —

phrases.aramaic: פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ עָשָׂה לָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: for this section the Holy One, Blessed be He, made
signs above and below it,
to say
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the section ויהי בנסוע, mentioned in step 26, as a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God marked off the section ויהי בנסוע with signs before and after it. The reason is given on the next amud.
